Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-22T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: tokenization budget, streaming semantics & SDK/auth follow-ups

Hi Alice — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the follow-up questions we promised to confirm so our engineering team can produce a short integration plan and sample code: 

Recap (today’s call)
- BrightOpt is evaluating streaming inference for a multi-turn assistant (customer support triage) with embedded reranker for clarification prompts.
- Key constraints: max per-request token budget ~ 4k input + response combined, audit-friendly complete user message preservation, and priority for latency under 300ms P95 for short responses (<= 150 tokens).

Specific questions for BrightOpt (answers will determine SDK/auth and routing recommendation):
1) Streaming semantics: do you need partial output as "delta" events (token deltas) or prefer periodic JSON chunks containing structured tool-call candidates? Which is easier for your frontend?
2) Stop behavior: are you relying on stop sequences (e.g., "\n---end---") to truncate model output, or prefer numeric max_tokens enforcement only? Any downstream parsers that will break on partial JSON?
3) Tokenization budget: do you count budget against input+output or do you have separate quotas (e.g., 3k input / 1k output)? Also confirm whether you need token-level accounting for audit logs.
4) Structured output & tool-calling: will you use the model to emit strict JSON (validated by schema) or will you post-process free text? If strict, please share the schema for our sample.
5) Embeddings/reranker: target embedding size (e.g., text-embedding-1024) and expected reranker throughput (queries/sec) so we can size batching.
6) Auth: preference between API key (short-term) vs mTLS or VPC/SAML for production. Any procurement constraints?
7) Routing: any mandatory region or failover policy (latency vs cost)?

Attachments: I’ve attached a short Redwood req/resp cheatsheet and a sample schema that illustrates streaming + tool-calling patterns we usually recommend.

Next steps: If you can reply inline to the numbered items above we’ll turn that into an internal integration plan + a 2-file sample (SDK snippet + request/response example) by Thursday.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Alice Ramirez <alice@brightopt.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-demo: tokenization budget, streaming semantics & SDK/auth follow-ups

Hi Vanessa — thanks for the clear recap. Answers below inline.

1) Streaming semantics: delta token stream is preferred for our UI (we render progressively). However, for tool-calling candidates we need complete JSON objects (not fragments). If Redwood can provide both (deltas + occasional full JSON events) that's ideal.
2) Stop behavior: we use stop sequences for certain templates. For the majority of safety-critical prompts we also enforce max_tokens. If a stop sequence appears mid-stream we want a guaranteed finalization event with the final JSON payload.
3) Tokenization budget: we enforce combined budget (input+output) with an upper bound of ~4k tokens per session. For audit we need token counts per request stored in our logs.
4) Structured output & tool-calling: we will use strict JSON for tool calls (schema attached as brightopt-tool-schema.json). Post-processing will be minimal.
5) Embeddings/reranker: prefer 1536-d embeddings; reranker expected peak 40 qps, baseline 5 qps. Batching is fine at up to 64 vectors.
6) Auth: for PoC we’ll use API keys, but production requires mTLS or customer-managed keys (KMS). Procurement requires proof of key rotation and audit logs.
7) Routing: primary region us-west-2; fallback to us-east-1. Cost is secondary to latency.

I attached a quick answers spreadsheet for SOC/security items as well. Happy to hop on a short follow-up if it helps.

Thanks,
Alice Ramirez
Platform Engineering
BrightOpt Solutions

Internal summary / engineering asks:
- UI needs delta streaming + finalization event containing validated JSON for any tool-calling. We should support a streaming mode that emits: DELTA (token fragments), JSON_EVENT (complete tool-call), FINAL (finalization + metadata).
- Stop seqs + max_tokens: ensure the runtime emits a FINAL event when a stop sequence is detected mid-stream (not just abrupt termination).
- Token accounting: include token counts in response metadata and expose per-request token cost in the SDK telemetry hooks.
- Embeddings: BrightOpt wants 1536d, up to 40 qps peak; recommend batching to 32-64 depending on latency SLO.
- Auth: PoC = API key; production = mTLS + KMS integration + key rotation proofs. We need a short one-pager for procurement describing rotation & audit logs.

Thanks — picking this up. Quick notes:
- DELTA + JSON_EVENT pattern is implementable at the SDK layer by tagging events (type: "delta" | "json_event" | "final"). Runtime will stream raw token deltas; SDK will buffer until a complete JSON_EVENT boundary and emit it atomically to consumer. This avoids partial-JSON parsing issues on the frontend.
- For stop sequences: runtime must emit a FINAL event with the final text + reason ("stop_sequence" | "max_tokens"). We can include token_count and model_hash in FINAL meta.
- Tokenization: we’ll add a telemetry header that returns token counts per message and cumulative session tokens; include an example response metadata block in the sample.
- Embeddings: will add a batching knob; for 1536d and 40 qps peak we’ll propose batching=32 with async backpressure to meet <50ms embed latency target where possible.
- Auth: SDK samples will show API key usage and an mTLS snippet (server cert config). Procurement one-pager: Vanessa — can you list specific KMS vendors/policies they require? I’ll draft the code samples today and aim to have a PR with examples by EOD Thursday.

Laura

Redwood Inference
